newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate seen rising - poll.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate seen rising - poll.

text.p: The Philippine benchmark 91-day treasury bill rate is seen jumping to 9.93 percent at the next auction on Monday from the previous week's 9.583, a Reuters poll of five financial institutions on Friday showed.
The expectations of higher interest rates were spurred by the lifting on Thursday of the Central Bank's overnight borrowing rate to 10 from 9.9 percent.
The poll showed the 182-day T-bill rate could rise to 10.2425 percent from 10.057; and the 364-day rate to 10.80 from 10.555 percent.
On Thursday, the Central Bank had also raised rates on the five-day reverse repo to 10 percent; the one-month reverse repo to 10.125; and the two-month reverse repo to 10.1875 percent.
All of these had previously carried a borrowing rate of 9.9 percent.
It also gave a higher rate of 10.25 percent on its six-month reverse repo from the previous 10.125 percent.
"Clearly, he (the central bank) had sent the signal for interest rates to move up," a foreign bank dealer said.
The Central Bank's action had been aimed at encouraging dollar inflows after domestic interest rates reached low levels and to curb outflows from stock market investments, dealers said.
"It's trying to protect the exchange rate," a dealer said.
Dealers also said the move was also intended to mop up liquidity after banks had been staying away from term reverse repos due to a new 20 percent tax imposed on interest income from the instrument.
A government official had earlier said the Central Bank had increased its borrowing rate because money supply ceilings had been edging closer to programmed ceilings.
Base and reserve money were 10 billion pesos below their targets in March and 20 billion pesos below in February, the Central Bank had reported.
A dealer said rates are expected to settle down in May after banks remitted to the government in late April billions of pesos in income tax payments.
